question.text: Ananya has NRE and NRO accounts. She invested Rs.10,00,000 in an equity fund through her NRE account and wants to redeem after 2 years. What is the key implication of the NRE account route?

answer.text: LTCG rate is lower for NRE account investments
NRE account investments are exempt from capital gains tax
Redemption proceeds are fully repatriable outside India since the original investment was from an NRE account
No TDS is deducted on NRE account investments

explanation.text: The Logic: NRIs invest through NRE or NRO accounts. The workbook treats NRE as repatriable and NRO as non-repatriable, and provides that purchases funded from NRE/FCNR accounts or from foreign exchange remittance can be paid on a repatriation basis. Redemption payment follows the source of purchase funds — NRE-funded units redeem on a repatriable basis, NRO/rupee-funded units do not. The Trap: The NRE route is about repatriation, not about a tax concession. NRI capital-gains TDS applies regardless of which account funded the purchase. Note: RTAs tag the source of funds at the unit level. Picking the right account at the investment stage is what preserves repatriation rights at redemption.
